the ZCT-QZVS concept is superior to the other concepts in terms of efficiency and power density.
the CF-ZVS and the ARCP converters are the most suitable candidates to be implemented in a high-voltage, high-power, low-voltage automotive dc-dc converter.

the comparison of the performance indices of the four different soft-switching converters.
the investigation of soft-switching techniques for bi-directional dc-dc converters and the development of analytical models to compare their performance in the context of automotive applications.
the development of a novel soft-switching converter concept, the ARCP converter, and its comparison with state of the art converters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of the considered converter specifications and technology node (120V/20A), the CF-ZVS-MLC converter is the best choice in terms of power density, efficiency and cost.

, although the CF-ZVS topology is the most efficient converter concept, the SAZZ topology offers the best trade-off between power density and efficiency, and is the best candidate for the next generation of automotive dc-dac converters.
the CF-ZVS- M topology is the most suitable topology for automotive applications, as it combines a high power density and a high efficiency with a low silicon area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CF-ZVS topology, with its high efficiency, compact size and low cost, is the most attractive solution for automotive power electronics applications.
the ZCT-QZV and CF-ZVS-M soft-switching converters are the most promising concepts, as they are capable to achieve high power densities and efficiencies, respectively.

the ARCP and the CF-ZVS converters are more suitable for high-power applications, whereas the ZCT-QZV and the ZCT-QVZT concepts are more appropriate for low power applications, and that the SAZZ topology is a compromise between these two extremes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soft-switching converters are a viable option to reduce the losses and to increase the efficiency of the automotive dc-dc converter.
the soft-switching converter concepts can be compared and evaluated with respect to their efficiency and power density by means of analytical models.
the CF-ZVS-ML converter is a promising topology, as the soft-switching concept allows for a significant increase of power density, while maintaining a high efficiency.
